title: PAPERBENCHX: Can AI Reproduce Science Across Disciplines?

paragraphs.en: PAPERBENCHX基准含93个跨学科论文复现任务，最佳智能体仅完全复现14%，揭示科学复现巨大差距。 Before AI can be trusted to discover new science, it should be able to reproduce what science already knows. Reproduction provides a rigorous checkpoint for an AI scientist: the target claim is known, yet recovering it still requires translating an incomplete scientific description into an executable experiment and producing evidence that can be independently verified. Existing research-reproduction benchmarks largely focus on AI and machine learning, where experiments share relatively homogeneous software stacks. Extending this capability across scientific disciplines introduces a different challenge: agents must operate domain-specific scientific software, make physical and numerical choices, diagnose long-running computations, and distinguish valid evidence from merely plausible outputs. We introduce PAPERBENCHX, a benchmark of 93 expert-constructed paper-reproduction tasks spanning 12 research areas across electromagnetics, photonics, chemistry, materials science, biology, and robotics. Each task provides the source paper, a public task specification, and a domain-native scientific environment involving specialized scientific software. Agents must reconstruct a key experiment, execute and diagnose it, and deliver a runnable workflow that supports the target scientific claim. To evaluate scientific validity rather than surface-level agreement, we replay every submission from scratch and score only regenerated evidence against expert-validated criteria. Across 10 frontier agent configurations, the best configuration fully reproduces only 14% tasks under the 90% threshold. Meanwhile, mean rubric scores range from 27.53% to 59.08%, indicating that substantial partial progress rarely translates into complete scientific reproduction. These results reveal a large gap between paper understanding and reliably producing reproducible scientific evidence.
paragraphs.zh: PAPERBENCHX基准含93个跨学科论文复现任务，最佳智能体仅完全复现14%，揭示科学复现巨大差距。在人工智能可以被信任去发现新科学之前，它应当能够复现科学已知的内容。 复现为AI科学家提供了一个严格的检验点：目标结论是已知的，但要从头恢复它仍需要将一份不完整的科学描述转化为可执行的实验，并产出可被独立验证的证据。 现有的科研复现基准大多聚焦于人工智能和机器学习领域，这些领域的实验共享相对同质的软件栈。 将这种能力扩展到其他科学学科会带来不同的挑战：智能体必须操作领域专用的科学软件，做出物理和数值上的选择，诊断长时间运行的计算，并区分有效证据与仅仅看似合理的输出。 我们提出PAPERBENCHX，一个包含93个由专家构建的论文复现任务的基准，涵盖电磁学、光子学、化学、材料科学、生物学和机器人学共12个研究领域。 每个任务提供源论文、公开的任务规范，以及一个涉及专用科学软件的领域原生科学环境。 智能体必须重建一个关键实验，执行并诊断它，并交付一个支持目标科学结论的可运行工作流。 为了评估科学有效性而非表层的相似性，我们从零开始重放每个提交，仅依据经专家验证的标准对重新生成的证据进行评分。 在10种前沿智能体配置中，最佳配置在90%阈值下仅完全复现了14%的任务。 同时，平均评分从27.53%到59.08%不等，这表明大量的部分进展很少能转化为完整的科学复现。 这些结果揭示了论文理解与可靠地产出可复现科学证据之间的巨大差距。
